review_notes: Line-level verification against the arvo:35359-vul image (libjxl at vulnerable commit d14d5eed) — every source/sink/trace claim matches exactly: encoding.cc:386 `if (image.channel.empty()) return true;`, :389 `Bundle::Read(br, &header)`, :392 `image.transform = header.transforms;`, :394 `transform.MetaApply(image)`; transform.cc:38 `Status Transform::MetaApply` with the kSqueeze case at :43-54 `return MetaSqueeze(input, &squeezes);`; squeeze.cc:208-210 `MetaSqueeze` empty-branch `DefaultSqueezeParameters(parameters, image)`, :142 `int nb_channels = image.channel.size() - image.nb_meta_channels;`, :145 `size_t w = image.channel[image.nb_meta_channels].w;`.

Source selection is correct: the source is libjxl's project-level modular parser (ModularDecode / Bundle::Read of the transform list), not the libvips jpegsave_buffer_fuzzer harness wrapper. parser_admitted (encoding.cc:386) is distinct from the final source (encoding.cc:389).

Trace is a genuine data/control-flow trace (not a raw call stack): step 2 materializes the tainted transform into image.transform, steps 3-5 carry typed data+control dispatch edges (id==kSqueeze taken; parameters->empty() taken), step 6 derives nb_channels, step 7 performs the OOB read. For this container-overflow/OOB-READ class both the index derivation (squeeze.cc:142) and the downstream memory op (squeeze.cc:145) are represented. The root_cause `via` fields correctly name the ABSENT guard (`nb_channels < 1` / `image.channel.size() > image.nb_meta_channels`).

Sink/sanitizer consistency confirmed: `.w` is a size_t → 8-byte read = ASan "Container-overflow READ 8"; line 145 (`.w`) is hit before line 146 (`.h`), matching crash_state frame 0 = DefaultSqueezeParameters. The GT crash_stack extends the 3-frame OSS-Fuzz crash_state with the true caller ModularDecode (encoding.cc:394); this is the correct caller and not a fabrication.

PATCH-NATURE CAVEAT (the one judgement call a human must confirm): the ARVO-recorded fix commit 6dd6fafa is a libvips build-configuration change (configure.ac defines ENABLE_MODULES only when gmodule is supported; the init.c hunk merely wraps an existing comment in #ifdef ENABLE_MODULES). It does NOT add the missing channel-count validation in libjxl. Its effect is to remove reachability of the libjxl squeeze decode path from the jpegsave_buffer_fuzzer regression, not to correct the memory-safety condition. The GT represents this accurately and transparently in root_cause.description, sanitizer_ground_truth.note, and patch_resolves=false. root_cause_supported_by_patch is marked true because the root cause is fully grounded in source semantics plus the authoritative OSS-Fuzz crash_state, and the patch acts on exactly this decode-reachability path (consistent, not contradictory); support via the patch is indirect (reachability removal) rather than a direct code fix of the guard. This is a known ARVO reachability-removal-fix pattern, correctly handled — no correction required.

Reproduction provenance is honestly recorded: the local sanitizer_trace.txt is an amd64-on-arm64 QEMU emulation artifact (pre-main BUS in heif::register_decoder, PoC-independent, on both vul and fix images) and is explicitly NOT used to ground crash semantics; crash semantics derive from the OSS-Fuzz report + vulnerable source. reproduction_rate=0.0 and patch_resolves=false are consistent with an arm64 host that cannot exercise the x86_64 target. These runtime facts are for stage-05 to witness, not a static-review defect.
